title: The coefficient module of one integral scalar residue layer
statement: Let O_L be the specified coefficient valuation ring, pi its specified uniformizer, and B=ULift(O_L/(pi^(n+1))). For 0≤j≤n the constant B-module sheaf of (pi^j B)/(pi^(j+1) B) is isomorphic to the restriction of the regular residue ring sheaf ULift(O_L/(pi)), along the actual quotient projection. The first quotient is a field. For every coefficient-field embedding E→L the completed scalar map followed by this residue projection equals the source residue projection followed by the induced first quotient map.

source.place: Modules on Sites, tensor cancellation (Tag 05V4), and Local Fields, Chapter I, section 1; residue-layer multiplication argument.

proof.text: The DVR witness says that the specified uniformizer generates the nonzero maximal ideal. Hence it is nonzero and its first quotient is a field. Quotient induction and the limit projection identities prove the scalar residue triangle.

Multiplication by the j-th uniformizer power surjects the truncated ring onto its j-th successive ideal layer. Lift to O_L and cancel the nonzero uniformizer power to show that the kernel equals that of the residue projection. The two first isomorphism theorems give the B-linear layer isomorphism.

Apply the constant module functor. Its comparison with restriction of the regular residue sheaf comes from the ring-sheafification unit, which is locally bijective. The induced map after additive sheafification is an isomorphism and hence so is the module-sheaf map.

proof_origin.description: Direct formalization of tensor balancing and the principal-ideal layer argument; no interval or constructibility assumption used in these comparisons.

mathlib_searches.query: Multiplication by a nonzero element power identifies consecutive principal ideal power quotients with the first quotient in a domain
mathlib_searches.results: Ideal.quotEquivPowQuotPowSucc and Ideal.powQuotPowSuccLinearEquivMapMkPowSuccPow cover the untruncated R-linear comparison. The proof below uses the first isomorphism theorem directly to retain the actual truncated-ring action.
LinearMap.quotKerEquivOfSurjective and its apply_mk and symm_apply lemmas. Used for the coefficient module isomorphism.
Mathlib principal-power quotient comparisons and Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso; project search found the proved natural tensor cancellation theorem.

      (ULift.{u + 1} (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l L (n + 1))))
    (hF : F = fun (j : Fin (n + 1 + 1)) ↦ (Ideal.span ({ULift.up ((Ideal.Quotient.mk
      (Padic.coefficientExtensionIdeal l L (n + 1)))
        (Padic.coefficientExtensionUniformizer l L))} :
          Set (ULift.{u + 1} (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l L (n + 1))))) ^ (j : ℕ))
    (j : Fin (n + 1)) :
    let B := ULift.{u + 1} (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l L (n + 1))
    Nonempty ((adicLisseConstantModules Y B).obj
      (ModuleCat.of B ((F j.castSucc) ⧸ (F j.succ).comap (F j.castSucc).subtype)) ≅
        (pbcRestrict (integralScalarResidueProjection l L Y n)).obj
          (SheafOfModules.unit (integralCoefficientSheaf l L Y 0)))
